title: Paper Gains From AI Stakes Inflate S&P 500 Earnings by Nearly 19 Points
excerpt: Unrealized gains from Alphabet's and Amazon's investments in Anthropic and SpaceX account for nearly half of the S&P 500's reported 47% earnings growth this quarter, masking a circular financing loop where Big Tech funds its own cloud demand.
body:
• S&P 500 earnings growth drops from 47.4% to 28.8% when Alphabet and Amazon's unrealized investment gains are stripped out, per FactSet data through July 31.
  • Alphabet booked roughly $99 billion in unrealized gains on its Anthropic and SpaceX stakes in Q2 — the same quarter it posted negative free cash flow for the first time in 22 years.
  • A circular financing pattern — hyperscalers invest in AI labs that commit to buying cloud compute from those same hyperscalers — is making headline earnings increasingly disconnected from cash generation.

The S&P 500's second-quarter earnings season looks spectacular on paper. Of the 305 companies that have reported so far, 86% beat estimates for earnings per share, above both five-year and ten-year averages, according to FactSet data released on July 31. Combined earnings growth stands at 47.4%.

Strip out two companies — Alphabet and Amazon — and the number falls to 28.8%. The 19-point gap comes almost entirely from unrealized gains on investments in companies that are themselves customers of the businesses reporting those gains.

Where the Gains Come From

Alphabet reported roughly $99 billion in unrealized gains during Q2, driven by surging valuations at Anthropic and SpaceX. The gains were folded into headline net income of $112 billion. The company did not separately disclose each investment's contribution.

https://x.com/Benzinga/status/2084671451026584015

In the same quarter, Alphabet spent $44.9 billion on capital expenditures — double the year-ago figure — and reported negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, its first such quarter in 22 years as a public company.

"The combined growth rate in earnings thus far is 47.4%, but drops to 28.8% excluding Alphabet and Amazon, both of which reported significant unrealized gains from their respective investments."

— FactSet Research, July 31 report

Amazon's Anthropic equity position — carried at roughly $74 billion as of March — contributed $12.3 billion to Q1 income from a single upward price adjustment. With Anthropic's valuation reportedly tripling during Q2, analysts expect another substantial mark-to-market gain in Amazon's forthcoming results.

Microsoft takes a different accounting route with its roughly 27% OpenAI stake. Under the equity method, it absorbs a share of OpenAI's operating losses directly. A $10 billion gain from OpenAI's October 2025 recapitalization boosted Microsoft's GAAP EPS by 60% in one quarter, prompting the company to promote adjusted earnings that strip the OpenAI effect out entirely, according to GeekWire.

The Closed Loop

What makes these gains unusual is the circular structure linking investor and investee. Anthropic has committed roughly $230 billion in compute purchases across the three major U.S. clouds: $100 billion to AWS over ten years, $30 billion to Microsoft Azure, and a multi-gigawatt arrangement with Google Cloud. OpenAI accounts for more than 40% of Microsoft's $625 billion in remaining cloud performance obligations.

The pattern works like this: hyperscalers invest equity in AI labs. The labs commit to long-term compute contracts with those same hyperscalers. The hyperscalers book the compute spend as cloud revenue and use it to justify the next round of capital expenditure. Rising private valuations then flow back as unrealized gains into the investors' earnings reports.

"Three companies, three instruments, one mechanism: the infrastructure costs more than the revenue base can fund, so the supplier finances its own demand."

— Lida Liberopoulou, independent researcher

Cash Tells a Different Story

While earnings soar on paper, free cash flow is moving in the opposite direction. Amazon's trailing twelve-month free cash flow fell 95% year-over-year to $1.2 billion through Q1. Morgan Stanley projects the full-year figure turning negative by roughly $17 billion. Meta's free cash flow narrowed to less than $1 billion in Q2, triggering a 9% stock drop.

The five major hyperscalers are on track to spend $755 billion on capital expenditure in 2026, an 83% jump, according to Goldman Sachs. To finance the buildout, Amazon has raised more than $50 billion in debt since late 2025, and Alphabet has issued over $30 billion in bonds. For the first time, hyperscalers collectively hold more debt than cash.

What's Next

Whether the circular financing pattern holds depends on Anthropic and OpenAI growing end-customer revenue fast enough to sustain their cloud commitments. Anthropic's annualized revenue jumped from $9 billion at end-2025 to $30 billion by April 2026, according to Bloomberg. OpenAI sits at around $24 billion. Both remain loss-making.

As both companies prepare for IPOs — Anthropic filed confidentially in early June, OpenAI followed days later — public markets will eventually evaluate them on audited financials rather than private valuations. Until then, paper gains from those valuations will continue to widen the gap between reported profits and actual cash generation across the S&P 500.
nri_angle: Indian investors with significant U.S. tech exposure through index funds and direct holdings should note that headline S&P 500 earnings growth is being inflated by non-cash gains, potentially masking deteriorating free cash flow at companies comprising a large share of global equity portfolios.
author: Diaspora Desk
